title: Index funds and costs

source.author: John C. Bogle
source.work: The Little Book of Common Sense Investing

principle: Most actively managed funds fail to beat the market after fees, and nobody can reliably tell you in advance which ones will. A low-cost fund that simply owns the whole market captures the market's return minus a tiny fee, and over decades that fee difference compounds into a very large gap. Costs are one of the few things about investing you can actually control.
fitsWhen: You're deciding where money allocated to the investing bucket should go, and want a default that doesn't require picking winners.
critique: Broad-market index funds still carry full market risk and offer no protection in a downturn; "low cost" is not the same as "low risk," and the approach says nothing about asset allocation across stocks, bonds or other classes.
